scope: Share discovery: exact creator-name search, daily top-20 snapshot, CSS type tiles. No production writes.

productionQueries.label: top20_plan
productionQueries.sql:
EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN WITH kinds(kind) AS (VALUES (?),(?),(?),(?),(?),(?),(?),(?),(?),(?),(?)),
 candidates AS MATERIALIZED (
   SELECT v.share_id, v.kind, v.view_count FROM kinds k CROSS JOIN my9_share_view_total_v1 v
   WHERE v.rowid IN (
     SELECT v2.rowid FROM my9_share_view_total_v1 v2
     JOIN my9_share_registry_v2 r2 ON r2.share_id = v2.share_id
     WHERE v2.kind = k.kind ORDER BY v2.view_count DESC, v2.share_id ASC LIMIT 20
   )
 ), top_shares AS MATERIALIZED (
   SELECT * FROM candidates ORDER BY view_count DESC, share_id ASC LIMIT 20
 )
 SELECT t.share_id, r.kind, t.view_count, r.creator_name, r.created_at
 FROM top_shares t JOIN my9_share_registry_v2 r ON r.share_id = t.share_id
 ORDER BY t.view_count DESC, t.share_id ASC

SEARCH r2 USING COVERING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_my9_share_registry_v2_1 (share_id=?)
USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY

1. Rows read measure how many rows a query reads (scans), regardless of the size of each row. For example, if you have a table with 5000 rows and run a `SELECT * FROM table` as a full table scan, this would count as 5,000 rows read. A query that filters on an [unindexed column](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/use-indexes/) may return fewer rows to your Worker, but is still required to read (scan) more rows to determine which subset to return.

2. Rows written measure how many rows were written to D1 database. Write operations include `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, and `DELETE`. Each of these operations contribute towards rows written. A query that `INSERT` 10 rows into a `users` table would count as 10 rows written.
4. Row size or the number of columns in a row does not impact how rows are counted. A row that is 1 KB and a row that is 100 KB both count as one row.

6. Indexes will add an additional written row when writes include the indexed column, as there are two rows written: one to the table itself, and one to the index. The performance benefit of an index and reduction in rows read will, in nearly all cases, offset this additional write.
8. Free limits reset daily at 00:00 UTC. Monthly included limits reset based on your monthly subscription renewal date, which is determined by the day you first subscribed.
9. There are no data transfer (egress) or throughput (bandwidth) charges for data accessed from D1.
Upgrading to the Workers Paid plan will remove these limits, typically within minutes.

The Workers Paid plan includes Workers, Pages Functions, Workers KV, Hyperdrive, and Durable Objects usage for a minimum charge of $5 USD per month for an account. The plan includes increased initial usage allotments, with clear charges for usage that exceeds the base plan. There are no additional charges for data transfer (egress) or throughput (bandwidth).

Users on the Workers Paid plan have access to the Standard usage model. Workers Enterprise accounts are billed based on the usage model specified in their contract. To switch to the Standard usage model, contact your Account Manager.

registryObservation.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total, SUM(creator_name IS NOT NULL AND creator_name <> '') AS named, SUM(CASE WHEN creator_name IS NOT NULL AND creator_name <> '' THEN length(CAST(creator_name AS BLOB)) ELSE 0 END) AS name_bytes, SUM(CASE WHEN creator_name IS NOT NULL AND creator_name <> '' THEN length(CAST(share_id AS BLOB)) ELSE 0 END) AS share_id_bytes, SUM(CASE WHEN creator_name IS NOT NULL AND creator_name <> '' THEN length(CAST(kind AS BLOB)) ELSE 0 END) AS kind_bytes, MAX(length(CAST(creator_name AS BLOB))) AS max_name_bytes, MAX(rowid) AS max_rowid, MIN(created_at) AS min_created_at, MAX(created_at) AS max_created_at, SUM(creator_name <> trim(creator_name)) AS untrimmed_names, SUM(CASE WHEN created_at >= ? AND created_at < ? THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS new_shares, SUM(CASE WHEN created_at >= ? AND created_at < ? AND creator_name IS NOT NULL AND creator_name <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS new_named_shares FROM my9_share_registry_v2

notes: All scenarios assume no edge-cache hits. Requests count actual network calls after page-local reuse.
CPU, new-index row metering, and new-index physical size are estimates, not post-implementation measurements.
Logs baseline and actual billing cycle are unavailable. CPU time is not SQL duration.
Account statistics are adaptive monitoring, not a precise invoice. August 19 through September 17 UTC excludes the September 18 cooccurrence rollout.
Storage covers index plus tiny snapshot at the planned initial size; monthly growth and other projects accumulate.
No new Analytics Engine events or queries for listing; detail-page traffic and subsequent saves are separate induced-load variables.
